description:
An empty XREFFILE that opens with '00', reads nothing, and whose CLOSE at :138 then reports the extended status '96'. INJECTED CONDITION: FILE STATUS '96' at the CLOSE call site, app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl:138. The frozen ParityCase schema carries no fault channel a batch case could use - ForcedOutcome belongs to ParityCase.ScreenRequest, and a BATCH_JOB case may not declare a screen - so the condition is named here in prose, arranged by the scenario table of CBACT03CParityTest, and pinned uniquely by the fingerprint below: 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' identifies the call site and 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9054' identifies the status. 9000-XREFFILE-CLOSE sets APPL-RESULT to 8 the long way round at :137, finds the status is not '00' at :139, takes the :141 arm and runs ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at :142, so 88 APPL-AOK is false at :144 and :147-150 run: DISPLAY 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE', 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, then 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. Four lines and RETURN-CODE 12; the abend at :158 carries the Language Environment arguments the paragraph sets immediately before it, ABCODE 999 at :157 and TIMING 0 at :156. Three things are pinned that no other case pins. First, the extended arm of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS is reached from the CLOSE paragraph as well as from the OPEN paragraph of case07, which is what makes the shared paragraph genuinely shared rather than incidentally correct at one site: '96' is numeric, but IO-STAT1 is '9', so :162 takes the arm at :164-168 - IO-STAT1 lands in IO-STATUS-04(1:1), TWO-BYTES-BINARY is zeroed at :165, IO-STAT2 is deposited into TWO-BYTES-RIGHT through the TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES at :54-56, and the code point of '6' is 54, which fills IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 as 054. The image is therefore 9054 and NOT 0096, and the NNNN ahead of it is part of the COBOL literal at :168 rather than a placeholder awaiting substitution - reproducing that oddity is required and correcting it would be a behaviour change. Second, the close ladder is exercised on a run that read nothing at all, so a translation that only closed after at least one successful read would produce two lines here instead of four. Third, there is no 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' line and no record line: CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :158 does not return, so :85 is unreachable on this and every other abend path, and an empty dataset offers :78 and :96 nothing to display. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion - the class is named AccountBalanceUpdateJob but CBACT03C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE and updates nothing - and expectedFinalState is empty because the dataset the run opened still holds no row. Every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by reading app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, app/jcl/READXREF.jcl and app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, never captured from a COBOL execution, because no runtime in this environment can execute these programs (AAP 0.7.6, risk R-A).

HOW THE FAULT IS INDUCED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a failed CLOSE whose status takes the extended-status arm: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names the call site CLOSE-XREFFILE and gives it FILE STATUS '96'. It is declared here because the identifier of a case must never configure it - a table in Java keyed by 'case01'..'case20' meant this file described three abend lines with nothing in it to say why, and renumbering a case silently changed what it did. A case that declares no call-site outcome runs clean, so silence here is itself a statement.
